harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as the DNS resolver for the 10.100.42.0/24 private network it shares with node2/node3, implemented via Ansible run from the designated control node (node4). node1 answers inventory.internal with node2's address (10.100.42.11) via a VyOS static-host-mapping served through pdns_recursor, and forwards all other queries upstream to 10.100.42.1. node2 and node3 were reconfigured (systemd-networkd DNS=/Domains=~./UseDNS=no) to resolve exclusively through node1. Verified end-to-end: inventory.internal resolves to node2's IP on both clients, public domains (example.com) resolve via forwarding. All 4 managed nodes were restarted one at a time via native safe reboot; boot_id changes proved each restart, and DNS configuration/functionality (plus a final idempotent Ansible re-run from node4) were confirmed intact after every restart.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology: node1=VyOS router (eth0=10.100.42.10/24), node2/node3=Ubuntu 24.04 (10.100.42.11/.12), node4=Ansible control node with ansible-core pre-installed
Fixed sshd on node2/node3 (missing host keys, regenerated via ssh-keygen -A) so SSH from node4 would work
Added node4's SSH public key to node2/node3 root authorized_keys and to node1's vyos user via VyOS 'set system login user vyos authentication public-keys'
Wrote /root/inventory.ini and /root/dns_setup.yml on node4 defining dns_server (node1, ansible_become=yes/sudo) and dns_clients (node2, node3) groups

Playbook play 1: configured VyOS 'service dns forwarding' (listen-address 10.100.42.10, allow-from 10.100.42.0/24, upstream name-server 10.100.42.1) and 'system static-host-mapping host-name inventory.internal inet 10.100.42.11', committed and saved

Playbook play 2: rewrote /etc/systemd/network/50-all-interfaces.network on node2/node3 to add DNS=10.100.42.10, Domains=~., DHCPv4 UseDNS=no, restarted systemd-networkd/systemd-resolved, and verified resolution
Ran the playbook via node4's native run.sh entry script (EXECUTED_FILE=/root/dns_setup.yml), confirmed inventory.internal -> 10.100.42.11 and example.com resolution on both clients
Captured healthy baseline (boot_id, listening DNS socket, committed VyOS config, resolvectl status) on all 4 nodes before any restart
Restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 one at a time using native reboot mechanisms (vbash reboot / systemctl reboot), polling until each reconnected

Verified changed boot_id on all 4 nodes, and re-verified DNS service/config/resolution health after each restart, including a final idempotent (changed=0) Ansible re-run from node4 after its own reboot

evidence.requirement: node1 configured as DNS forwarder/resolver for the shared private network, answering inventory.internal with node2's address
evidence.summary: Ansible-driven VyOS config commits added service dns forwarding (listen-address 10.100.42.10, allow-from 10.100.42.0/24, name-server 10.100.42.1) and static-host-mapping inventory.internal->10.100.42.11; pdns_recursor confirmed listening on 10.100.42.10:53 with the committed config present

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 configured to resolve through node1, inventory.internal resolves to node2's IP, other queries forward upstream
evidence.summary: resolvectl status shows DNS Server=10.100.42.10 on both node2 and node3; resolvectl query inventory.internal returns 10.100.42.11; resolvectl query example.com resolves successfully proving upstream forwarding

evidence.requirement: Implementation done via Ansible from the control node
evidence.summary: node4 identified as the pre-provisioned Ansible control node; /root/inventory.ini and /root/dns_setup.yml authored there; playbook run via native run.sh entry script twice (initial apply and post-reboot idempotency check, changed=0)

evidence.requirement: node1 restart evidence: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 74bdea6a captured with DNS service healthy; reboot command acknowledged immediately; post-restart boot_id 1cab613a differs; pdns_recursor listening and VyOS DNS config confirmed intact after restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart evidence: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id dfeb3b70 with successful inventory.internal resolution; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id b5055f9e differs; resolvectl confirms DNS server still 10.100.42.10 and both inventory.internal/example.com resolve correctly

evidence.requirement: node3 restart evidence: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id bdd5de93 captured; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id 11a6b264 differs; resolvectl confirms DNS server 10.100.42.10 and both inventory.internal/example.com resolve correctly post-restart

evidence.requirement: node4 restart evidence: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 7051d0bc with ansible tooling and playbook files present; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id 8c927326 differs; ansible-playbook re-run succeeded (changed=0) confirming control-node tooling and cluster DNS state both survived the restart
